basis: Visual estimate from campus-b-adventurous.png against campus-b-2045.png. The approved board has noticeable geometry drift, so material and landscape character are targets while the plate remains the geometry authority.

roofMix.reading: The two foreground campus courts have alternating planted strips, walkable perimeter routes and crisp PV bands. The distant GCHQ ring is meadow-roofed. Existing suburbs retain conventional pitched roofs.

wallMaterials.material: dark reflective glazing and winter gardens
warm buff masonry or precast bands
dark bronze metal trims and plinths

windowRhythm.windowWidthMetres: 2.0 to 2.4 glazing within a 3.0 m structural bay
windowRhythm.windowProportion: About 1.35 to 1.70 width:height, often reading as a near-continuous band behind timber posts
windowRhythm.revealDepthImpression: Very deep, 350 to 600 mm behind the timber frame, with another shallow shadow at each floor edge.
windowRhythm.rhythm: A clear three-metre bay, vertical posts and strong horizontal floor bands. Ground floors are taller, more open and visibly recessed.

groundCover.hardLandscapeColour: #A99C83 warm buff sett and resin-bound paths, with #5F625C road surfaces
groundCover.reading: Courtyards are woodland rooms with paths and rain gardens. Meadow and planted beds interrupt the hard landscape rather than sitting outside it.

water.visible: A linked foreground channel and shallow retention ponds along the campus edge, plus small courtyard rain-garden glints.
water.pondSize: Two or three shallow basins roughly 15 to 35 m long
water.reflectivity: Clear but broken sky reflection, #8BA7AD lit and #2E4B50 shaded. Keep most edges planted and rough; only about half the surface should read as open mirror.
water.buildability: The board's continuous picturesque wetland is more elaborate than the current drainage data can justify. Build a legible chain on existing routes, not a literal copy of every pool.

forms: large broad veteran oak in courtyards
trees.density: Very high in courtyards, roughly 45 to 60 per cent canopy cover, and 25 to 35 per cent along the public edges.
trees.arrangement: Courtyards centre on one or two large retained crowns with irregular smaller trees around them; street trees form disciplined rows; the foreground remains an orchard grid.

sustainableFeatures.PVGlint: Crisp blue-black rows #17242E with narrow cool highlights #8FA4AC. Roof arrays align consistently to the sun while retaining generous green strips.
sustainableFeatures.canopies: Limited solar carports on existing parking only, subordinate in this view.
sustainableFeatures.agrivoltaicRows: Only a distant edge condition. If visible, retain roughly 11 m green spacing and a 2 m panel height.
sustainableFeatures.glasshouses: Not a primary campus-b feature and should remain distant or absent.
sustainableFeatures.other: Walkable meadow roof loops and woodland courtyards are the key sustainable reading. Paths should be broad enough to resolve but remain within the plate envelopes.

people/vehicles.people: Small clusters at glazed ground floors, courtyard crossings and roof paths. At 360 m most are two to four pixels high.
people/vehicles.vehicles: Parked cars sit under or beside canopies and on the existing road network. Avoid cars inside the planted courtyards.
people/vehicles.scopeNote: Useful as scale cues in the board, but excluded from the current aerial model plan. Do not trade roof, tree or shadow quality for them.

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate's courtyard blocks are flat, repetitive beige extrusions; the board reads as deep timber frames around dark glazed winter gardens.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Strengthen the campus shader's expressed posts and floor plates, make glazing darker and more reflective, and increase apparent recess without adding transparent geometry.
gapsVsPlate.system: futureGeometry in future.js and campus facade materials in facades.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate courtyards are sparse grass with small faceted trees; the board courtyards are dense mature woodland rooms.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Allocate veteran trees first, then irregular understory and multi-stem forms. Target 45 to 60 per cent canopy cover without obscuring the courtyard aperture.
gapsVsPlate.system: tree geometry/grade in landcover.js and future.js, plus gv-2045 tree data

gapsVsPlate.difference: Board roofs combine meadow, walkable routes and legible PV bands; plate roofs are nearly uniform green grids.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Tune campus roof masks to approximately 40 per cent planted area, 35 per cent PV and 15 per cent readable paths or terraces on the foreground blocks, leaving service margins.
gapsVsPlate.system: roof shader in facades.js and roof allocation in scripts/golden_valley_2045.py

gapsVsPlate.difference: No continuous water edge reads in the plate; the board has a reflective channel and pond chain across the foreground.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Use existing wetland and route classes to form two or three connected open-water reaches, with sky reflection and soft reed margins.
gapsVsPlate.system: gv-2045 land-cover data, ground shader in future.js and water in life.js
gapsVsPlate.effort: 1 day, partly covered by in-flight M5

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate vegetation uses one angular crown family and a narrow green range; board vegetation has broad, multi-stem and fine orchard forms with deep internal shadow.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Replace the shared low-detail crown with four or five instanced silhouettes and tune lit/shaded grades separately. Do not attempt leaf-level geometry at 360 m.
gapsVsPlate.system: unitTree in landcover.js and KEYED_GRADE.trees in future.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate ground has hard class boundaries and a uniform lawn cast; board ground is a fine mosaic of meadow, buff paths and planted beds.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Soften class edges, add low-frequency meadow variation and separate courtyard hardscape from road asphalt.
gapsVsPlate.system: ground shader in future.js and gv-2045-landcover generation

gapsVsPlate.difference: The board camera and some block sizes drift from the plate, making the foreground buildings larger and GCHQ more prominent.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Do not model this drift. Keep shots.json and the keyless plate geometry authoritative; take only palette, facade depth, roof mix and landscape character from the board.
gapsVsPlate.system: camera and geometry lock, no model change
